title: The Repository of Unseen Things

features.name: the shelf of absence
features.desc-on-touch: shelves holding empty space with care—each gap labeled, each void indexed, the archive storing the shape of what cannot be seen

features.name: the labeled void
features.desc-on-touch: a box with a handwritten label, its contents invisible—the label is more real than whatever it contains or fails to contain

features.name: the unseen eye
features.desc-on-touch: an eye rendered in profile, its iris covered by a petal or membrane—what it sees remains unknown to the archive, which can only store the fact of the seeing

features.name: the redacted filing
features.desc-on-touch: papers with black bars across text—the metadata intact, the content removed—proof of what cannot be seen

reverie.title: REVERIE — the thing you could not look at
narr: She stands in the doorway. You are afraid to ask
what she has seen. The wall between you is just
the air—you cannot cross it because she has not
told you it is there. She keeps one hand open.
The fear shapes itself around her silence. You
know now that what you cannot see has always been

exits.label: back toward the fear-shaped question that brought you here
deeper into the chambers where the archive questions what it cannot know
toward chambers where things refuse to let themselves be seen
